item.title: #3594880: FlowDrop: editing a workflow in FlowDrop's editor silently makes it unusable for ai_eval again
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +83/−10 · php +67/−3 · md +16/−7
  • Diff: ac7fea9
  • Discussion: #3594880 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The ai_eval_flowdrop submodule previously told users the Drush command that makes a FlowDrop workflow synchronous would survive later saves in FlowDrop's editor. That was wrong for saves that change a node's settings, such as a system prompt. The editor removes metadata.orchestrator_settings, and ai_eval then refuses the next run. The README, the ai-eval-flowdrop skill and the "cannot run" reason shown on the target form now say to run the command again after such an edit. Model steps from flowdrop_ai_provider (Chat, Simple Chat and similar) are now recorded as AI steps instead of other. Entity Query and the session history step are recorded as deterministic.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In FlowDropRunReader, the step kind is derived from the executor plugin id (provider:base[:...]). The provider is now checked before the data_* and text_* prefix rules, because some text_* executors from flowdrop_ai_provider also call a model. Any flowdrop_ai_provider executor maps to WorkflowStep::KIND_AI, except session_history, which reads memory and maps to KIND_DETERMINISTIC. entity_query was added to the KINDS map as deterministic. Unknown providers still fall through to KIND_OTHER.

FlowDropWorkflowRunner::asynchronousReason() appends a sentence saying the FlowDrop editor removes the orchestrator setting when node settings are edited and saved. The same text appears in the exception message for refused launches. Kernel tests cover the executor id to kind mapping (including session_history and an unknown provider), a real Entity Query run, and the new reason text. The docs also gain a troubleshooting row and a note on a FlowDrop 2.7.2 Prompt Template limit: printing a list variable fails with "Render context is empty", so loop over it and print a field instead. The issue says the root cause of the setting being dropped is in FlowDrop and would be reported there.

Upgrade

After editing node settings of a FlowDrop workflow in the editor, run the command again:

drush config:set flowdrop_workflow.flowdrop_workflow.WORKFLOW_ID \
  metadata.orchestrator_settings.type flowdrop_runtime:synchronous -y

Use flowdrop_stategraph:stategraph instead for workflows that call tools.

item.title: #3616124: Saving the anonymous user (uid 0) revokes access tokens for any consumer with an unset/anonymous default user
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 6.1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +661/−40 · php +661/−40
  • Diff: 721409f
  • Discussion: #3616124 · 9 contributors · 38 comments
  • Followers: 10
  • AI disclosures: 3 of 9 contributors

Summary

Saving the anonymous user (uid 0) no longer deletes OAuth tokens belonging to real users on consumers that have no default user. Saving a user who is a consumer's default user also no longer revokes other users' access tokens on that consumer. Tokens that actually authenticate as the saved user are still revoked, and refresh tokens are still kept. If you have custom code that relied on the old behavior of sweeping a default user's consumer tokens, use collectForClient() instead.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ExpiredCollector::collectForAccount() now returns only non-refresh tokens that authenticate as the account (explicit subject, or no/deleted subject on a Consumer defaulting to it) and returns [] for the anonymous account. TokenExpiryTriggerHandler::handleUserUpdate() ignores the anonymous account.

Technical details

simple_oauth_user_update() fires on every user save, including uid 0, and called ExpiredCollector::collectForAccount(). That method collected tokens by auth_user_id and then every token of any Consumer whose default user_id matched the account. The fix leaves the hook unchanged. TokenExpiryTriggerHandler::handleUserUpdate() now returns early for anonymous users, and collectForAccount() returns [] for them.

collectForAccount() now runs two queries. The first selects non-refresh tokens whose auth_user_id is the account. The second selects non-refresh tokens of Consumers defaulting to the account that have no existing user, using notExists('auth_user_id.entity.uid'). That covers tokens with no subject or a deleted subject, which fall back to the Consumer's default user. Tokens whose explicit subject is another existing user are skipped. The QueryException case when loading consumers by user_id now falls back to the first query's results only.

The collector queries in collect(), collectForAccount() and collectForClient() now use accessCheck(FALSE), since they are internal and not run on behalf of a user. The issue notes this means cron deletes expired tokens owned by any account. A reviewer found no query access handler on oauth2_token, so this was not filtering anything before. The anonymous skip lives in the default handler, which is a replaceable service from #2946882; a custom handler must add its own check. Refresh tokens are not revoked on user or consumer saves, consistent with #3436728, which rejects refresh grants for unpublished consumers.

Upgrade

If custom code called ExpiredCollector::collectForAccount() expecting every access token of a Consumer whose default user is the account, call collectForClient() for those consumers instead:

$tokens = $collector->collectForClient($consumer);

If you replaced the TokenExpiryTriggerHandlerInterface service, add your own $user->isAnonymous() check in handleUserUpdate().

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: August 11, 2026
  • Committed: November 6, 2026 (2 months later)

Key contributors

  • benstallings (Encore Healthcare)
  • scott falconer (Acquia)
  • pfrilling (Pare & Co)
  • mglaman (Acquia)
  • attilatilman (Acquia)
  • alex ua (Zivtech)
  • e0ipso (Lullabot)
  • bojan_dev

Collaboration

Scott Falconer pointed out early that a uid 0 guard alone missed the root cause: collectForAccount() could revoke other users' tokens for any Consumer default user, and he extended the MR to cover that. Pfrilling then drove the review, reworking the design. A credential-change gate in the handler was tried and later dropped so the default handler only skips the anonymous account, and the refresh token purge update hook was removed. Alex UA's runtime retest with real authorization_code tokens exposed that refresh-token revocation on the consumer side could not reach real refresh tokens, which fed into that rework.

item.title: #3586785: HostnameFilter HTML-encodes & and > in Markdown output
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +437/−16 · php +412/−16 · md +25
  • Diff: 85d52a8
  • Discussion: #3586785 · 1 contributor · 17 comments

Summary

The AI module's hostname filter no longer turns & into & and > into > in text that has no HTML. Chat answers written in Markdown (quote blocks, code spans, tables) now come through unchanged. Plain-text mode no longer breaks Markdown links. A disallowed link is reduced to its text, and an allowed link keeps its closing parenthesis. Text that really does contain HTML tags is still filtered as before. An opt-in Markdown mode is available for consumers that render Markdown and want HTML examples inside code spans and blocks preserved.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New markdownMode property on HostnameFilterDto and new HostnameFilter::setMarkdownMode() method; snapshotSettings()/restoreSettings() now include markdownMode.

Technical details

The encoding came from HostnameFilter::filterText() always round-tripping text through the HTML5 parser, which encodes text nodes. After the Markdown link pass, it now returns early when the new containsHtmlMarkup() check finds no HTML. That check looks for < followed by a letter, /, ! or ?. It also treats invalid UTF-8 as HTML, because the HTML parser drops invalid bytes before tokenizing and so could hide a tag with an invalid byte after the < from the check. By default any <tag counts as markup, including inside backticks or indented code, since an HTML consumer would still act on it.

When markdownMode is TRUE, containsHtmlMarkup() parses the text with a League CommonMark parser, without rendering it. It reports HTML only if it finds an HtmlBlock, an HtmlInline, or a Text node containing a tag-like sequence. Autolinks, reference destinations and code therefore skip the HTML round trip. Plain-text mode takes precedence over Markdown mode. Mixed Markdown and HTML can still be HTML-encoded.

In plain-text mode, filterMarkdownLinks() now runs before the bare-URL pass, with $allow_rewrite = FALSE so a disallowed link is always reduced to its text and never rewritten. It also takes $preserve_mailto = TRUE, which keeps mailto: links, autolinks and reference definitions as plain-text mode already did for bare URLs. The bare-URL replacement now keeps trailing punctuation when it removes a URL. markdownMode is also handled by applySettings(), snapshotSettings() and restoreSettings(). The README gains a "Markdown consumers" section.

Upgrade

Only enable this if your consumer renders the output as Markdown:

use Drupal\ai\Dto\HostnameFilterDto;

$chatInput->setHostnameFilter(new HostnameFilterDto(markdownMode: TRUE));

For direct service calls, use $hostnameFilter->setMarkdownMode(TRUE). The service is shared, so restore the previous settings afterwards with snapshotSettings() and restoreSettings().

item.title: #3586786: createDuplicate() throws TypeError on AI config entities (non-nullable $id)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +199/−12 · php +199/−12
  • Diff: ab20054
  • Discussion: #3586786 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

Duplicating AI config entities (assistants, guardrails, guardrail sets, prompts, prompt types, automators, automator tools and automator chain types) with the entity API's createDuplicate() no longer crashes with a TypeError. Code that clones these entities, including contrib modules such as Entity Clone, now gets an unsaved copy with no ID and a new UUID.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

EntityBase::createDuplicate() sets the ID key of the clone to NULL. The eight entity classes declared protected string $id;, so that assignment failed. Each now declares protected ?string $id = NULL;, matching core config entities. The affected classes are AiGuardrail, AiGuardrailSet, AiPrompt, AiPromptType, AiAssistant, AiAutomator, AutomatorsTool and AutomatorChainType. id() already returns string|int|null, so the public API does not change. The commit adds three kernel tests (ConfigEntityDuplicateTest, AiAssistantDuplicateTest, AutomatorEntityDuplicateTest). They call createDuplicate() on each entity type and assert that the ID is null, the UUID differs and the original keeps its ID. I did not check whether other code reads $this->id directly and assumes a string. The issue lists that as a remaining task, and the diff does not touch such code.

item.title: #3594879: A FlowDrop workflow built in the FlowDrop editor does not appear in the target form
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 26 files, +836/−23 · php +644/−17 · md +192/−6
  • Diff: d93957c
  • Discussion: #3594879 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

A workflow built in FlowDrop's editor used to be missing from the ai_eval target form, with only a generic "no available workflows" message. The cause is that the editor stores no orchestrator, so FlowDrop runs it in the background, and ai_eval can't wait for the answer. The target form now lists the workflows an engine can't run, with a reason. For FlowDrop the reason includes the Drush command that sets a synchronous orchestrator. The FlowDrop engine now has a proper label and checks the question port, fixed inputs, output path and an ignored provider or model when you save a target. Question port choices read "Title (name)", and a single allowed port is preselected. Steps on the results page show the canvas title with the node id. The README, the ai-eval skill and a new ai-eval-flowdrop skill document the extra FlowDrop modules a workflow needs and how to set the orchestrator.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: WorkflowRunnerDetailsInterface::unavailableWorkflows() returns hidden workflows keyed by id with a label and reason. WorkflowStep gets an optional label constructor argument.

Technical details

WorkflowRunnerDetailsInterface (the optional interface, unreleased) gains unavailableWorkflows(). It returns [id => ['label' => ..., 'reason' => ...]] and must never include anything listWorkflows() returns. EvalTargetForm calls it when the runner implements the interface. With listed workflows present it renders a closed details element titled "Not listed (N)" below the Workflow select. With none, it adds the list to the notice ("No workflow from this engine can run yet."). Labels and reasons are cast to strings and passed through @ placeholders, so engine text is escaped. If a saved target's workflow is hidden, the notice includes the reason.

Runners report what their lists already skip. AI Prompt reports a missing prompt type or a type with no variables. AI Automators reports automators whose load() throws a refusal. Search API reports disabled indexes or indexes without an enabled server. AI Answers returns [].

FlowDropWorkflowRunner now implements WorkflowRunnerDetailsInterface. label() returns "FlowDrop". unavailableWorkflows() returns asynchronous workflows with the Drush config:set ... metadata.orchestrator_settings.type flowdrop_runtime:synchronous reason. questionPorts() goes through the new FlowDropRunReader::questionPorts(), which uses FlowDrop's SchemaFragmentChecker::checkValue() on the declared type, so FlowDrop's own rules apply. An enum is only checked per question at launch. validateTarget() and run() share bindingErrors(). It checks that the question port is declared (and typed for text at save time), that fixed inputs are declared and don't include the question port, that the output path starts with a declared output name, and that no provider or model is set (FlowDrop ignores them). run() now loads the workflow through runnableWorkflow(), which throws the same asynchronous reason text.

WorkflowStep has a new optional label. FlowDropRunReader sets it only when the canvas title differs from the node id. WorkflowRecordMapper stores it as a capped label key only when present. The workflow panel shows Label (node_id).

In the form, question port options become "Title (name)" when they differ. A sole allowed port is used as the default and pinned after an AJAX reset.

Upgrade

Custom workflow runners that implement WorkflowRunnerDetailsInterface must add the new method. Return [] if nothing is hidden:

public function unavailableWorkflows(): array {
  return [];
}

To explain a hidden workflow, return ['workflow_id' => ['label' => $label, 'reason' => $reason]]. The workflow must not also appear in listWorkflows(). To show a node label on the results page, pass label: when building a WorkflowStep.

item.title: #3594878: Set up a workflow target in the target form
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 23 files, +1985/−123 · php +1895/−90 · md +90/−33
  • Diff: 4420b86
  • Discussion: #3594878 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Workflow targets can now be created and edited in the AI Eval target form instead of only through YAML import. When at least one workflow runner is installed, the add form offers a Workflow mode. You pick the engine, then the workflow, then the input that receives the question. The lists refresh in place as you change the engine or workflow. You can also enter fixed inputs as YAML and set an output path. Chat provider and model settings now apply in workflow mode too, which AI Prompt needs. The form checks the engine, workflow, question port and fixed inputs on save, and shows a message if a runner fails to list its workflows or ports. Existing agent and chat targets cannot be switched to Workflow. Config YAML is still the export and import format.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New optional Drupal\ai_eval\Workflow\WorkflowRunnerDetailsInterface (label(), questionPorts(), validateTarget()) and WorkflowRunnerCollector::label(). WorkflowRunnerInterface is unchanged.

Technical details

EvalTargetForm gains engine, workflow and question port selects with htmx redraws. A workflow with no declared ports gets a text field for the port. Per the shipped docs, the redraws go through the form's own route and permission, so no separate fragment routes were added. On save the form writes the workflow keys, keeps the stored workflow_snapshot (the form has no field for it), and returns form errors before the entity throws. Those errors cover an uninstalled engine, an unlisted workflow (a new check), an undeclared or disallowed question port, fixed inputs that name an undeclared port, and fixed inputs that name the question port.

The new optional WorkflowRunnerDetailsInterface sits next to WorkflowRunnerInterface. label() gives the engine name. questionPorts($workflowId) returns the ports that can take the question, NULL for any declared port, or an empty list for none. validateTarget() takes the workflow id, question port, fixed inputs, output path, provider id and model id. It returns errors keyed by workflow_input_port, workflow_inputs, workflow_output_path or provider_model. A runner that implements only WorkflowRunnerInterface still works: WorkflowRunnerCollector::label() falls back to the engine id, and every declared port is allowed.

All four shipped runners implement the interface. AI Answers allows only question. Search API allows only keys. AI Automators allows every declared port except text_format. AI Prompt allows only declared variables that have a single-brace placeholder in the prompt. To keep save-time and run-time checks the same, each runner's run() checks were moved into shared private helpers (for example validateInputs() and validateModel()). PromptRenderer::validateValues() and UnsavedEntityBuilder::validateTextFormat() were extracted for the same reason. AI Automators now rejects a non-empty output path at save time. AI Prompt requires both a provider and a model. The docs in docs/user/usage/targets.md and docs/user/developers/index.md were updated.

Upgrade

Optional for custom workflow runners. Implement Drupal\ai_eval\Workflow\WorkflowRunnerDetailsInterface alongside WorkflowRunnerInterface to get a label and question port filtering in the target form:

final class MyRunner implements WorkflowRunnerInterface, WorkflowRunnerDetailsInterface {
  public function label(): \Stringable {
    return new TranslatableMarkup('My engine');
  }
  public function questionPorts(string $workflowId): ?array {
    return ['question'];
  }
  public function validateTarget(string $workflowId, string $questionPort, array $fixedInputs, ?string $outputPath, ?string $providerId, ?string $modelId): array {
    return [];
  }
}

Runners that do not implement it keep working: the form shows the engine id and allows any declared port.

item.title: #3594876: Add a FlowDrop runner for workflow mode
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 16 files, +1978/−14 · php +1765/−12 · md +169/−2 · yml +40 · txt +2 · json +2
  • Diff: 14d4f8b
  • Discussion: #3594876 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

AI Eval gets a fifth workflow-mode runner, in the new ai_eval_flowdrop submodule. With it, a target with workflow_engine: flowdrop runs a synchronous FlowDrop workflow once per question. The workflow's declared output is graded as the answer. Each FlowDrop job shows up as a step on the result page, and each individual tool invocation is available to tool-use checks and judges. Asynchronous workflows are not listed or run, because ai_eval waits for each answer. Paused, failed or cancelled runs supply no answer. The workflow really runs and its writes are saved, so use a test copy of the site for workflows that write.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: ai_eval_flowdrop needs drupal/flowdrop ^2.7.2 (added to require-dev and suggest) and its flowdrop_workflow_executor module.
  • New API: New ai_eval_flowdrop submodule with an ai_eval.workflow_runner service (id flowdrop) and ToolCallRecord::fromParts() for engines whose tool calls are plain arrays.

Technical details

FlowDropWorkflowRunner (id flowdrop) is tagged ai_eval.workflow_runner. It checks that the caller has execute flowdrop_workflow and a view own or view any flowdrop_pipeline permission. It refuses a missing or asynchronous workflow with WorkflowLaunchRefusedException, then launches through flowdrop_workflow_executor.launcher with LaunchOptions(wait: TRUE) and never relaunches. listWorkflows() only lists workflows whose resolved orchestrator is not asynchronous. Model calls are recorded through ai_eval.model_call_recorder while the workflow runs.

All reads of FlowDrop internals sit in one adapter, FlowDropRunReader, which reloads the pipeline through FlowDrop's storage registry. Declared outputs come from the last completed graph job of each node, passed to WorkflowSchemaResolverInterface::extractOutputs(). Without workflow_output_path, one declared output is used. With several, the single output marked turn: reply wins, otherwise the named-output map is encoded as JSON. A missing output is reported as an error, not as an empty answer. Booleans become true or false, and structures become JSON.

Steps are ordered by execution_order metadata, then start time and job id, with skipped jobs last. Kinds come from the node type's executor plugin: reason is ai, tool_invoke is tool, flowdrop_workflow and workflow_executor are subflow, a list of known logic nodes is deterministic, and anything else is other. The attempt is retry_count + 1. Previews are redacted and capped at 500 characters. Jobs marked tool_invocation become tool-call records and nest under the consumer job named in invoked_by. The batch tool_invoke job is a step but not a call record. Child pipelines are matched to subflow jobs by exact parent pipeline id, in order. If the counts differ, the children have no parent execution id and a note is added. Following child pipelines stops after eight levels.

To share the redaction and caps, ToolCallRecord::fromFunctionCall() now delegates to a new public ToolCallRecord::fromParts(), and redactOutput() became public. A unit test checks the two paths give identical records. The README says that with FlowDrop 2.7.2 a launched workflow's tools reach tool_invoke only on the stategraph orchestrator. It also says FlowDrop 3.0.0 moves the optional job lookup methods, so the supported range is stated as ^2.7.2.

Upgrade

To use it, install FlowDrop and enable the submodule:

composer require 'drupal/flowdrop:^2.7.2'
drush en ai_eval_flowdrop

Then configure a workflow target in YAML, for example:

mode: workflow
workflow_engine: flowdrop
workflow_id: answer_question
workflow_input_port: question
workflow_output_path: ''

item.title: #3583056: Validate the declared constraints on list and map outputs
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +382/−100 · php +382/−100
  • Diff: a6ff119
  • Discussion: #3583056 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

Constraints declared on list and map outputs, such as Count with min or max, are now enforced when a tool's outputs are validated. Before, they were advertised but never checked. This also covers outputs declared with the deprecated multiple: TRUE, which the shim converts to a list. Tool authors may see new output violations where a list or map has the wrong number of items or properties. A required list or map with no Count still accepts an empty value.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: ValueViolationsTrait::validateDeclaredConstraints() now accepts input or output definitions, so TypedOutputsTrait can use it too.

Technical details

validateOutputValue() in TypedOutputsTrait now calls validateDeclaredConstraints() after it has walked the items of a list or the properties of a map. Only the author-declared constraints run, not the typed-data defaults, so an empty required collection stays valid unless Count says otherwise. Each declared constraint is validated against its own freshly created data as a non-root call. This stops core's validator from descending into members and reporting each member fault twice. The prototype reset guard (#3616328) applies. A misdeclared constraint, for example Count with no options, throws, as it does on the input side (#3583048). For maps, an exception from a constraint is dropped only if the property walk already reported a violation, so the walk's violation rejects the value.

The helper moved from TypedInputsTrait to ValueViolationsTrait. Its $definition parameter is now typed InputDefinitionInterface|OutputDefinitionInterface, so inputs and outputs share it. New kernel tests in TypedOutputsTest cover lists, maps, a map without properties, a converted multiple output, empty values, and an invalid declaration. The map test is skipped on core below 11, which recurses into map properties and entity fields on a non-root validation with explicit constraints (#3583093).

item.title: #3583054: Cast form values once at extraction instead of returning raw form strings
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +282/−2 · php +282/−2
  • Diff: a1f34bc
  • Discussion: #3583054 · 1 contributor · 11 comments

Summary

When a tool is run from its execute form, a field left empty now means "not set". The tool's configured value applies, and if there is none, the input's default applies. Before this fix, an empty field was passed as an explicit empty input and skipped the configured value. The fix ships with kernel tests that check the values the tool actually receives, not the raw form values.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In ExecuteToolPluginForm, the shared extraction step for validation and submission now reads the typed value after extractFormValues(). It calls $this->plugin->setInputValue() only when that value is not NULL. An explicit NULL input would resolve straight to the default and bypass configuration. An input set before the form keeps its value.

The configure form is unaffected. Clearing a stored field there still resets it to the default, which a test covers. An unchecked checkbox still reaches the tool as FALSE, so a configured TRUE does not win.

The commit adds a form_values_tool test plugin in tool_test and a kernel test, ToolPluginFormValuesTest. The test covers numeric strings becoming int or float, checkbox handling, empty execute fields falling back to configuration, and the configure form clearing a stored value. The type casting described in the issue title comes from the existing typed data extraction. This diff only changes the NULL handling.

item.title: #3594871: Let the groundedness and accuracy judges see what an agent's tools returned
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +701/−45 · php +641/−28 · md +58/−17 · txt +2
  • Diff: 276e198
  • Discussion: #3594871 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

For agent tests, the Groundedness judge now sees what the agent's tools returned, not just which tools ran. It can check a stated value, such as a tuition figure, against the actual tool result instead of passing any answer that follows a search. Each call's output is capped at 4,000 characters and the whole output section at 12,000. The newest outputs are kept and omitted ones are named. The Accuracy judge still sees only call names and arguments. Outputs are not stored or exported, but a judge's stored reason may quote part of one. If the AI module's logging is on, it will log the judge prompt with the tool data. Judge prompts for these tests are longer, so they use more tokens.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: No stored config changes. Groundedness judge prompts for agent tests get longer, which raises judge token use.
  • New API: New sees_tool_output property on the AiEvalGrader attribute (requires sees_tool_calls), and optional output and output_cut keys on tool call records.

Technical details

ToolCallRecord::fromFunctionCall() now reads getReadableOutput() when the tool implements ExecutableFunctionCallInterface. It stores output, cut to OUTPUT_MAX_LENGTH (4000) characters, plus output_cut when shortened. If the accessor throws, the record keeps its identifiers and arguments and omits the output. Redaction is name-based and runs on the first OUTPUT_SCAN_LENGTH (16,000) raw characters. It does not decode JSON, so numbers and key order are preserved. JSON-style values under secret-looking keys become "(redacted)". Plain key: value and key=value lines whose key matches the argument secret-name rules are also redacted. A secret under an innocuous name is not caught.

Code outside a tool call can now get the schema of a value object whose members are marked with #[ToolProperty]. A new tool.value_object_describer service returns the same definition a tool output of that class would get. You can turn it into JSON Schema with the serializer. It builds an @internal TypedMethodDescriber and calls a new describeValueObject() on it. That method reuses the private valueObjectOutput() that tool outputs go through, so the schemas match (kernel tests compare against real tool outputs). It reflects the class only, so it needs no instance and calls no getters.

The optional $members argument takes the same selection syntax as #[ToolOutput(members: ...)]: names, named ToolProperty refinements, and names keyed to nested lists. An explicit selection can also include unmarked public properties and getters. The result is a required, non-nullable map labelled with the humanized short class name.

$definition = $describer->describe(Image::class);

item.title: #3583116: Pass the invoker to method-tool `access` callbacks
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +125/−14 · php +92/−11 · md +33/−3
  • Diff: 9f187b6
  • Discussion: #3583116 · 1 contributor · 15 comments

Summary

Tools declared with #[ToolMethod] can now make their access decision depend on who is invoking them. Before, only #[Tool] plugins could see the invoker, so a tool that had to be disabled for certain callers could not be written as a method tool. Existing access callbacks that take two parameters keep working unchanged.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: #[ToolMethod] access callbacks are now called with a third argument, the nullable ?Invoker set on the tool: (array $values, AccountInterface $account, ?Invoker $invoker).

Technical details

MethodTool::checkAccess() now calls the declared access method as $this->service->{$method}($values, $account, $this->getInvoker()). getInvoker() returns NULL when the tool was created without an invoker, for example from Tool Explorer or ToolManager::createInstance() with no invoker. PHP ignores the extra argument for callbacks that declare only two parameters, which is why they are not affected. ToolRunner::run() supplies the invoker ID php when its caller omits one, and drush tool:run supplies drush (both per the updated docs).

The docs and the ToolMethod attribute docblock describe the new signature. They also note that an ID comparison does not reliably identify remote callers. Caller-kind capabilities are tracked in a separate issue, #3583130. The documented example returns AccessResult::allowedIf(...)->setCacheMaxAge(0), because the result depends on the invoker and the runner does not cache access results. The change adds an InvokerAccessFixture test fixture and kernel tests covering a set invoker, a different invoker and NULL.

Upgrade

Optional. To use the invoker, add a third parameter to the access callback:

use Drupal\tool\Tool\Invoker;

public function invokerAccess(array $values, AccountInterface $account, ?Invoker $invoker): AccessResultInterface {
  return AccessResult::allowedIf($invoker?->id === 'example_caller')
    ->setCacheMaxAge(0);
}

item.title: #3583095: Let tool results declare cache tags, contexts, and max-age
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +490/−1 · php +467/−1 · md +23
  • Diff: 0203701
  • Discussion: #3583095 · 1 contributor · 17 comments

Summary

Tool results can now carry cache tags, cache contexts and a max-age, so consumers such as MCP resources, render caching or AI response caching can cache read-only tool output safely. Results stay uncacheable (max-age 0) unless the tool declares what it read, so existing tools behave as before. Failed results are always uncacheable.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Any custom implementation of ToolResultInterface must now implement getCacheContexts(), getCacheTags() and getCacheMaxAge().
  • New API: ToolResultInterface now extends CacheableDependencyInterface; ExecutableResult::withCacheableDependency() added.

Technical details

Cacheability sits on the result, not the tool, because the same tool returns different data for different inputs. This is the follow-up to #3582965, which removed CacheableDependencyInterface from ToolInterface.

ExecutableResult gets an optional CacheableMetadata and withCacheableDependency(object $dependency). It merges CacheableMetadata::createFromObject($dependency) into the existing metadata and returns a new instance, since the class is final readonly. With nothing declared, getCacheMaxAge() returns 0. The first declared dependency makes the result cacheable, and the merge then takes the lowest max-age. An object that isn't cacheable keeps the result at 0. A tool that depends on nothing it loaded can pass an empty CacheableMetadata to make the result permanent. getCacheMaxAge() also returns 0 for failures, though tags and contexts still pass through.

FormattedExecutableResult delegates tags and contexts to the original result. Its max-age is 0 when formatting replaced a ContentEntityInterface with a handle, checked recursively through arrays. Handles are stored in the current user's tempstore, so a cached copy would hand out a handle that was never stored. The raw result stays cacheable. Access cacheability is not copied into the result, so consumers merge the access result's cacheability themselves. Docs in creating-a-tool.md and the method-tools page are updated. A cacheable_node_tool test plugin and kernel and unit tests are added.

Upgrade

In a tool's doExecute(), declare what the result depends on:

return ExecutableResult::success(
  new TranslatableMarkup('Loaded the node.'),
  ['title' => $node->label()],
)->withCacheableDependency($node);

Custom classes implementing ToolResultInterface need to add getCacheContexts(), getCacheTags() and getCacheMaxAge().

item.title: #3583090: Narrow validateInputValue()'s catch so unexpected exceptions do not reach callers as violation text
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +129/−4 · php +129/−4
  • Diff: 9adf62b
  • Discussion: #3583090 · 1 contributor · 11 comments

Summary

Tool input validation no longer passes the message of any exception to the caller as if it were a problem with the input. Previously an unexpected error during validation, such as an unknown constraint listing every constraint plugin ID, or a database error carrying SQL, could reach an LLM over MCP, the AI connector, the CLI or a form. Now only genuine "this value can't be held by this type" rejections are reported as input violations. Other errors are logged. The caller sees a generic failure naming only the exception type, or a generic access denial.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: validateInputs() can now throw unexpected exceptions (e.g. PluginNotFoundException for an unknown constraint) instead of converting every \Exception into a violation; direct callers must handle them.

Technical details

In TypedInputsTrait::validateInputValue() the typed-data branch's catch (\Exception $e) is narrowed to \InvalidArgumentException | UnexpectedTypeException. These are the structural rejects, such as an array given for a string, and their messages are still turned into a ConstraintViolation. Anything else now propagates out of validateInputs().

Propagated exceptions are handled by the existing paths. ToolBase::execute() catches \Throwable, logs it, and returns a Runtime failure with the message Tool execution failed: <ExceptionClass>. The full error has been logged. (the Runtime-failure message comes from #3583121, referenced in the test docblocks). In ToolBase::access() a new catch (\Throwable $e) logs via Error::logException() and returns AccessResult::forbidden('Tool input validation failed.') with max-age 0, so access fails closed without exposing the detail.

Tests cover an unknown constraint (NoSuchConstraint, throwing PluginNotFoundException) in TypedInputsValidationTest (exception propagates, Runtime failure, access forbidden and logged once) and in ToolRunnerTest, where ToolRunner::run() returns a Runtime failure and logs once.

Upgrade

Code calling validateInputs() directly, outside ToolBase::execute() or ToolRunner, should expect exceptions other than \InvalidArgumentException and UnexpectedTypeException to propagate rather than appear as violations.
